import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Convert Dt_Customer to datetime
df['Dt_Customer'] = pd.to_datetime(df['Dt_Customer'], format='%d-%m-%Y')

# Create a new column for total spending
df['Total_Spending'] = df[['MntWines', 'MntFruits', 'MntMeatProducts', 
                           'MntFishProducts', 'MntSweetProducts', 'MntGoldProds']].sum(axis=1)

# Create a new column for number of children

# Set the style of seaborn

# Create a figure and axis

# Plot a boxplot of Total Spending by Education level

# Set the title and labels

plt.xlabel('Education Level', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Total Spending', fontsize=12)
plt.xticks(rotation=45)

import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Convert Dt_Customer to datetime
df['Dt_Customer'] = pd.to_datetime(df['Dt_Customer'], format='%d-%m-%Y')

# Create a new column for total spending
df['Total_Spending'] = df[['MntWines', 'MntFruits', 'MntMeatProducts', 
                           'MntFishProducts', 'MntSweetProducts', 'MntGoldProds']].sum(axis=1)

# Create a new column for number of children
df['Children'] = df['Kidhome'] + df['Teenhome']

# Set the style of seaborn
sns.set(style='whitegrid')

# Create a figure and axis
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))

# Plot a boxplot of Total Spending by Education level
sns.boxplot(x='Education', y='Total_Spending', data=df, palette='muted')

# Set the title and labels
plt.title('Total Spending by Education Level', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Education Level', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Total Spending', fontsize=12)
plt.xticks(rotation=45)

# Save the plot as a file
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
